qt: to the Commission Aldo Patriciello (PfE) Subject:

The increasingly frequent use of artificial intelligence in production processes and administration highlights the need to bridge the digital divide among small and medium-sized enterprises and public administration by leveraging automation and analytics tools. The absence of structured training pathways could hamper the competitiveness and efficiency of public services, thereby harming the European economic fabric. The failure to promptly implement coordinated measures is likely to exacerbate territorial and technological disparities, thereby preventing small companies from accessing global markets and keeping up with modern digital efficiency standards. In the light of the above, could the Commission clarify whether it will develop funded training programmes and common guidelines to support the secure uptake of AI by SMEs and public administration?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.11.2026) To support integration of AI and digital transformation of small and medium-sized enterprises, mid-caps and public sector organisations the Commission has initiated the establishment of the network of European Digital Innovation Hubs counting more than 200 hubs across EU and other European Countries. Since December 2025, the European Digital Innovation Hubs are Experience Centres for AI supporting the adoption of sector-specific AI solutions, while also providing services such as training services to upskill and reskill the European Workers. The European Digital Innovation Hubs facilitate further companies’ access to other initiatives in the European AI innovation ecosystem. The European Digital Innovation Hubs are co-financed by the Commission. The Commission further supports the development of AI digital skills, including training targeting specifically the needs of SMEs and public administration through for example the Digital Europe Programme1. The Commission also revised the European Digital Competence Framework (DigComp 3.0) in November 2025, to better integrate AI across all 21 competences of DigComp2. A key initiative is the newly established AI Skills Academy that will help build and expand Europe’s AI talent base by bring together and offer a broad range of AI-related training opportunities for different target groups and sectors. Individual Learning Accounts3 can further support adult learning, including in the digital domain. The Commission has also adopted4 and is preparing5 guidelines on the practical implementation of the AI Act that help facilitate compliance with the AI Act for, among others, small and medium-sized enterprises and public sector organisations.
